mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a consistent week-over-week improvement (-13.7 to -10.9) over the last four weeks, indicating positive momentum in discretionary outings. This momentum is expected to persist, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:monotonic improvement from -13.7 to -10.9 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to continue its upward trend and instead declines or plateaus for two or more consecutive weeks following the snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -6.0 (i.e., recovers more than 2 points past its current -5.3 level), it signals renewed use of public transit for commuting and shopping trips, which should translate into higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks as transit-dependent shoppers resume in-person retail visits.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -6.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -9.4 to -5.3 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses the threshold but RETAIL_REC does not rise, or rises by less than 1 point, within the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates loosening of mobility restrictions and resumption of normal commuting-linked activity patterns; when both rise together, the compounded effect on foot traffic near workplaces and transit hubs drives a stronger increase in RETAIL_REC than either series would predict alone over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks is no greater than what WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone would predict via their individual historical correlation, indicating no synergistic interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The recent decline and partial rebound in PARKS (from -12.0 to -17.0 then to -14.6) reflects a seasonal transition where outdoor activity is becoming less weather-favorable; as outdoor substitution options shrink, some of that foregone park activity shifts toward indoor retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -12.0 to -17.0 then partially recovered to -14.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and PARKS move in the same direction (both decline or both rise together) rather than showing the hypothesized inverse substitution pattern.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility (above +30 percent) reflects persistent errand-running behavior that frequently bundles with nearby retail visits; as households continue combining grocery and retail trips, RETAIL_REC should rise modestly within one week as a downstream co-visitation effect.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose steadily from 31.6 to 37.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise but RETAIL_REC does not increase within the following week, breaking the assumed co-visitation link.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 5.5 (down from its current stable 6.0-7.3 range), it would indicate households are spending measurably less time at home, a leading behavioral indicator that typically precedes a broad-based increase in out-of-home activities including retail and recreation within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL drops below 5.5 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has remained stable between 6.0 and 7.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL crosses below 5.5 but RETAIL_REC does not rise, or declines, within the subsequent four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Under a regime of tightening restrictions, a simultaneous weekly decline in WORKPLACES and rise in RESIDENTIAL would jointly signal renewed stay-at-home policy enforcement, which should suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as discretionary outings are curtailed in response to combined labor-market and home-confinement signals.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL have both shown volatility in recent weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL move in the triggering combination but RETAIL_REC does not decline, or instead rises, over the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: During a steady-state seasonal regime with no major outdoor weather disruption, the current modest and gradual PARKS recovery (from -17.0 to -14.6) indicates stabilizing outdoor-activity patterns that typically coincide with stabilizing, slightly improving retail traffic, producing a small positive shift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -17.0 to -14.6 in the most recent week
failure_condition: PARKS continues to recover but RETAIL_REC stagnates or declines over the next four weeks, indicating decoupling of the two series.
